paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: when God gives a word, He finishes what He said. Jabin gathered a crowd "as numerous as the sand on the seashore," with horses and chariots on top (Joshua 11:4). Then the LORD told Joshua, "Do not be afraid of them…" (Joshua 11:6). The size of the enemy didn't change what God had said, and that's worth carrying into your Monday.

Now look at how Joshua answered. The text says he left "nothing undone of all that the LORD had commanded Moses" (Joshua 11:15). He didn't pick the easy parts and skip the rest. And it wasn't a one-afternoon job either, because "Joshua waged war against all these kings for a long period of time" (Joshua 11:18). Obeying God can be slow, friend, and I know a thing or two about waiting, so I'm telling you: keep going.

This chapter is also heavy, and I'll say that once and plainly. But the ending is where the promise lands: "So Joshua took the entire land, in keeping with all that the LORD had spoken to Moses," and "the land had rest from war" (Joshua 11:23). God said it, God did it, and God gave rest. So bring your fears to Him, baker, and keep trusting the One who keeps His word.
